visualChecks.check: Workspace tree row iconography and Dark readability

visualChecks.actual: The selected System Map row includes the digest-owned left indicator and visible marker; the semantic collection records exactly one active-row non-colour indicator.

maskRationale: The single declared selector is accepted only for the visible official Excalidraw SDK editor interior. The review did not exclude the Pinned Sidebar, top Tabs, Sidebar/Back controls, Workspace header, tree rows, row icons, divider, or any app-owned shell perimeter. The High mismatch lies in an unmasked Workspace tree region.

findings.screenState: 06 · Workspace · Pinned · Dark / Workspace tree disclosure, directory, and drawing glyphs
findings.expected: Workspace row iconography remains recognizable and readable in Dark mode. The approved baseline shows light disclosure/folder/drawing glyphs; the component contract requires distinct 16x16 icons and the Dark semantic direction uses #CED4DA secondary foreground on #232329 panels.
findings.actual: The fixed visual actual renders the Workspace tree disclosure, folder, and drawing glyphs near black. Pixel inspection of the unmasked glyph regions shows dominant non-background values #000000 and #111114, which visually collapse into the #232329 panel and remain too dark on the #403E6A selected row. The text and selected-row indicator remain readable, but the hierarchy and drawing/directory identity icons do not.
findings.reproduction: Open the manifest-verified workspace-pinned-dark.png and the fixed visual actual.png separately at native 1280x760. Inspect the unmasked Workspace tree from approximately x=16..76 and y=140..274, covering the root and nested disclosure chevrons, directory icons, and drawing icons. Compare their foreground separation against the baseline and the #CED4DA Dark secondary foreground contract.
